title: Diagnostic utility and accuracy of 68Gallium FAPI PET/CT in patients with TESTicular germ cell tumors – the prospective phase Ib FAPI-TEST study
summary:
Overall, germ cell tumors are a rare tumor entity that primarily affects young patients. Currently, staging is performed using CT or MRI; if metastases are detected, chemotherapy or surgical intervention is undertaken. Since CT or MRI cannot always reliably differentiate between malignant and benign findings, there is a need for imaging with high accuracy for this purpose.
Therefore, this study includes patients with localized germ cell tumors with risk factors, metastatic disease, or residual tissue after chemotherapy. These patients undergo a 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT in addition to conventional imaging, in order to subsequently assess the diagnostic value of 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT.

interventions.name: Patients with germ cell tumors in the metastatic stage, with residual disease after chemotherapy, or with localized disease but high-risk factors, receive a 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT after being informed and giving consent.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
seminoma and non seminoma patients:
Clinical Stage: I (high risk and unfavourable histology), IIA, IIB, residual mass after chemotherapy
Exclusion criteria:
non willingness to enter the study
age < 18
